name: 18 · Explaining detections and SOC processes · Natural English
description: 100 microescenarios revisados para explicar detecciones, datos, alertas, correlación, falsos positivos, triaje, escalado, monitorización, limitaciones y próximos pasos con un inglés claro, natural y prudente. El contexto SOC apoya el aprendizaje lingüístico; ninguna respuesta depende de una decisión técnica discutible.

questions.question: You are introducing a detection rule to a customer. Which opening sounds clearest?
options: This rule proves that unusual sign-ins are malicious whenever it generates an alert.
This rule has the purpose of making the identification of sign-ins that are unusual.
This rule identifies every suspicious sign-in and confirms whether the account is compromised.
This rule is designed to identify unusual sign-in patterns that may require investigation.
questions.explanation: La estructura «is designed to identify» explica la finalidad con claridad sin prometer certeza. «Proves», «every» y «confirms» exageran; «has the purpose of making the identification» es innecesariamente pesada.
questions.translation: Esta regla está diseñada para identificar patrones de inicio de sesión inusuales que pueden requerir investigación.

questions.question: Complete the sentence for a client briefing: 'The main purpose of this use case is ___.'
options: highlighting all activity which definitely represents an attack
for highlighting activity so that every threat can be confirmed
to highlight activity that deserves a closer look
that it highlights activities deserving to be looked more closely
questions.explanation: Después de «the purpose ... is» resulta natural usar «to + infinitive». «Deserves a closer look» es una colocación idiomática y prudente.
questions.translation: El objetivo principal de este caso de uso es destacar la actividad que merece un análisis más detenido.

questions.question: A slide says, 'The rule detects impossible travel.' You want to make the claim more precise when speaking. Which version is best?
options: The rule detects impossible travel and therefore establishes that the account was attacked.
The rule looks for sign-ins from locations that appear inconsistent with the time between them.
The rule is looking at locations because travel between them could be impossible for the user.
The rule searches impossible journeys, which normally means that somebody stole the credentials.
questions.explanation: «Looks for» describe el patrón buscado sin convertir una alerta en una conclusión. «Appear inconsistent» mantiene el nivel de certeza adecuado y suena natural.
questions.translation: La regla busca inicios de sesión desde ubicaciones que parecen incompatibles con el tiempo transcurrido entre ellos.

questions.question: Which sentence distinguishes the rule's objective from its outcome most naturally?
options: The rule is intended to surface suspicious behavior; the investigation determines what the behavior means.
The objective of the rule is surfacing behavior, and its outcome determines the incident completely.
The rule intends that suspicious behavior surfaces, while analysts are deciding its final meaning.
The rule finds suspicious behavior, so the outcome is an incident unless an analyst rejects it.
questions.explanation: «Is intended to» expresa finalidad y el punto y coma separa dos ideas relacionadas. La frase evita atribuir a la regla una conclusión que corresponde a la investigación.
questions.translation: La regla pretende sacar a la luz comportamientos sospechosos; la investigación determina qué significan.

questions.question: During a call, you need to explain that a detection has a narrow scope. Choose the most natural sentence.
options: This detection is focused in changes that happen to groups with privileged membership.
This detection focuses specifically on changes to privileged group membership.
This detection controls all privileged activity.
This detection has a narrow scope because it only detects every change made by privileged users.
questions.explanation: La colocación correcta es «focuses on», no «focuses in». «Specifically» delimita el alcance de forma directa y natural.
questions.translation: Esta detección se centra específicamente en los cambios en la pertenencia a grupos privilegiados.

questions.question: A customer asks what a rule is meant to catch. Which response works best in spoken English?
options: It's meant to flag repeated failures followed by a successful sign-in.
It is meant for flagging failures repeatedly and then a sign-in that has success.
It confirms an account takeover after a successful sign-in.
Its meaning is to flag repeated failures, after which success in the sign-in is observed.
questions.explanation: «Be meant to + infinitive» es una forma oral y natural de explicar la finalidad. La respuesta describe el patrón, no una conclusión técnica absoluta.
questions.translation: Está pensada para señalar fallos repetidos seguidos de un inicio de sesión correcto.

questions.question: Select the best customer-friendly explanation of a threshold-based rule.
options: The alert is triggered when the number of failed attempts exceeds the configured threshold.
The alert triggers when failed attempts are more than what the threshold has configured.
The configured threshold makes the alert trigger and confirms that the attempts are hostile.
Once failures exceed any normal number, the alert will always be triggered as an incident.
questions.explanation: «Is triggered when ... exceeds the threshold» usa una pasiva muy habitual para explicar reglas. Las otras opciones tienen colocaciones poco naturales o añaden certeza injustificada.
questions.translation: La alerta se activa cuando el número de intentos fallidos supera el umbral configurado.

questions.question: You want to explain that the rule does not inspect message content. Which sentence is clearest?
options: The rule analyzes the metadata of messages, but it does not look inside of their actual contents.
The rule analyzes message metadata, not the content of the messages themselves.
The rule sees only metadata, so message content stays completely private.
The rule does not inspect contents because metadata is all the information it needs to decide.
questions.explanation: El contraste «metadata, not the content ... themselves» es conciso y enfático. Evita garantías o conclusiones que no hacen falta para explicar el alcance.
questions.translation: La regla analiza los metadatos de los mensajes, no el contenido de los propios mensajes.

questions.question: Which phrase is the most natural way to introduce an example of activity covered by a rule?
options: For example, the rule can flag a new forwarding setting created shortly after a suspicious sign-in.
As an example, the rule can confirm a compromise when any forwarding setting is newly created.
For putting an example, a forwarding setting after a sign-in is something the rule can flag.
By example, the rule flags forwarding settings, which are suspicious after all sign-ins.
questions.explanation: «For example» introduce el caso de manera idiomática. «Can flag» expresa capacidad sin afirmar que el ejemplo confirma un compromiso.
questions.translation: Por ejemplo, la regla puede señalar una nueva configuración de reenvío creada poco después de un inicio de sesión sospechoso.

questions.question: A technical description is too dense for a meeting. Choose the best spoken version.
options: Simplifying the terminology, a sequence of anomalous events is evaluated in relation to the entity during the current review.
Basically, the rule knows when the account is behaving maliciously across a sequence of events.
Said in simple terms, events are sequenced so unusual behavior will be conclusively identified.
In simple terms, the rule looks for a sequence of events that would be unusual for this account.
questions.explanation: «In simple terms» funciona como marcador oral y «would be unusual» añade prudencia. La frase reduce densidad sin perder el significado.
questions.translation: Dicho de forma sencilla, la regla busca una secuencia de eventos que sería inusual para esta cuenta.

questions.question: You need to name the data used by a detection without sounding overly technical. Which sentence is best?
options: The detection consumes sign-ins together with devices for making more context available.
The detection uses all identity data, so visibility is complete.
The detection uses sign-in and device data to provide additional context.
The detection provides context by taking every sign-in and device event as evidence.
questions.explanation: «Uses X and Y data to provide context» es una estructura clara y natural. «Consumes» es más técnico y las otras opciones exageran la cobertura.
questions.translation: La detección utiliza datos de inicios de sesión y dispositivos para aportar contexto adicional.

questions.question: Complete the update: 'At the moment, we are not receiving ___ from two servers.'
options: the audit logs that we expected to be received by us
all telemetry, which prevents any form of investigation
the expected audit logs
those expected logging informations
questions.explanation: «The expected audit logs» es conciso; «logs» es contable, mientras que «information» sería incontable. La frase informa de una carencia concreta sin generalizar.
questions.translation: En este momento no estamos recibiendo los registros de auditoría esperados de dos servidores.

questions.question: A customer asks whether the SOC can see every action. Choose the most professional answer.
options: We see nearly everything across the monitored environment, so any action not shown in our tools probably did not happen at all.
Our visibility is good, although saying what we cannot see is technically not possible.
We cannot see every action, which means that the monitoring has little value for this review.
We have good visibility in the monitored systems, but it would be inaccurate to say that we can see every action.
questions.explanation: «It would be inaccurate to say...» corrige una expectativa con tacto. El contraste «but» permite reconocer la cobertura sin prometer visibilidad total.
questions.translation: Tenemos buena visibilidad en los sistemas monitorizados, pero no sería exacto decir que podemos ver todas las acciones.

questions.question: Which sentence explains a temporary data gap most naturally?
options: There is a logging gap, and therefore nothing reliable can be said about the complete investigation or the wider incident timeline.
There is a gap in the logs between 02:10 and 02:35, so our view of that period is incomplete.
The logs have a hole from 02:10 until 02:35, making the period impossible to understand.
We are missing every log between 02:10 and 02:35, so no activity happened in that period.
questions.explanation: «A gap in the logs» y «our view ... is incomplete» son colocaciones naturales. La consecuencia se limita al periodo afectado, sin sacar conclusiones extremas.
questions.translation: Hay un vacío en los registros entre las 02:10 y las 02:35, por lo que nuestra visión de ese periodo es incompleta.

questions.question: During a presentation, how should you explain that one source adds useful detail?
options: Endpoint data helps us understand what happened on the device after the sign-in.
Endpoint data helps us to understand with certainty everything that happened after signing in.
The endpoint information is helping us for understanding the subsequent device happenings.
Endpoint data completes the sign-in evidence and turns the alert into a confirmed incident.
questions.explanation: «Helps us understand» no necesita «to» y suena natural. La frase explica la contribución de la fuente sin afirmar que resuelve todo el caso.
questions.translation: Los datos del endpoint nos ayudan a entender qué ocurrió en el dispositivo después del inicio de sesión.

questions.question: Choose the clearest way to say that a source was unavailable when the alert fired.
options: That source of data had not availability at the moment the alert was generating.
That data source was not available when the alert was generated.
The source was unavailable, which proves the alert was wrong.
The alert generated itself without that source, so its findings are not usable now.
questions.explanation: La pasiva «was generated» y la expresión «was not available» sitúan dos hechos pasados con claridad. No se infiere una consecuencia que el contexto no aporta.
questions.translation: Esa fuente de datos no estaba disponible cuando se generó la alerta.

questions.question: A client asks why two dashboards show different counts. Which response is most natural?
options: They use data sources and time windows differently, making both figures technically wrong.
The figures are not directly comparable because each dashboard has decided on another version of the truth.
They use different data sources and time windows, so the figures are not directly comparable.
Different sources produce different counts, so we should choose whichever figure is higher.
questions.explanation: «Not directly comparable» es una expresión habitual para matizar comparaciones. «So» conecta causa y consecuencia de forma clara.
questions.translation: Utilizan fuentes de datos y periodos diferentes, por lo que las cifras no son directamente comparables.

questions.question: You want to request missing logs politely. Select the best wording.
options: You must send the missing logs now because the review cannot continue in any way.
Would you be able to provide all logs, which we need to prove what happened conclusively?
Could you share the logs for that period so that we can complete the review?
Can you facilitate us the logs of that period for being able to complete the revision?
questions.explanation: «Could you...?» formula una petición cortés. «So that we can...» expresa el propósito; «facilitate us» y «revision» son calcos poco naturales.
questions.translation: ¿Podríais compartir los registros de ese periodo para que podamos completar la revisión?

questions.question: Which version best explains that retention limits the historical review?
options: Because these logs are retained for 30 days, we cannot use them to review activity from earlier in the year.
Due to the logs retaining 30 days, reviewing activity from earlier in the year is not currently possible for us.
As the logs are kept for 30 days, there cannot have been relevant activity before that period.
The 30-day retention means that historical activity is outside the rule's responsibility.
questions.explanation: «Are retained for 30 days» y «cannot use them to review» explican la limitación con una relación causal clara, sin confundir ausencia de datos con ausencia de actividad.
questions.translation: Como estos registros se conservan durante 30 días, no podemos utilizarlos para revisar actividad de principios de año.

questions.question: The customer asks what 'coverage' means here. Which explanation is clearest?
options: Coverage means that the detection monitors the environment and covers any activity of interest.
Here, coverage is when systems and activities have been put under a detecting capability.
Here, coverage means the systems and types of activity that the detection is able to monitor.
Coverage refers to the percentage of threats that the rule will detect successfully without any misses at all.
questions.explanation: La definición usa «means» y una relativa sencilla. Delimita el término a sistemas y tipos de actividad, evitando promesas absolutas.
questions.translation: Aquí, cobertura se refiere a los sistemas y tipos de actividad que la detección puede monitorizar.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: A customer treats every alert as a confirmed attack. Which correction is most tactful?
options: An alert is a signal that needs to be assessed; it is not, by itself, confirmation of an attack.
An alert is only a possibility, so it should never be treated by itself as reliable confirmation of an attack.
You are confusing an alert with an attack, and those terms do not mean the same thing.
Alerts are not attacks unless the SOC changes their status to confirmed incidents.
questions.explanation: El punto y coma equilibra definición y contraste. «Not, by itself» corrige la idea con precisión y sin sonar brusco.
questions.translation: Una alerta es una señal que debe evaluarse; por sí sola, no confirma un ataque.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: Choose the most natural way to explain that several events belong together.
options: These events appear to be related, so we are reviewing them as part of the same investigation.
These events are related for sure, which is why they form one confirmed incident.
The events have relation among them, so one investigation is currently being made about all of them together.
We grouped the events because related events always represent a single incident.
questions.explanation: «Appear to be related» expresa una conclusión provisional y «as part of» es una colocación natural. La frase no convierte la agrupación en certeza.
questions.translation: Estos eventos parecen estar relacionados, así que los estamos revisando como parte de la misma investigación.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: Complete the client update: 'We have opened an investigation, but we have not yet ___.'
options: confirmed the account to have a compromise occurring
confirmed that the account was compromised
made the confirmation of a compromised account
classified every account alert as malicious
questions.explanation: Con «confirm», la estructura natural es «confirm that + clause». «Not yet» encaja con present perfect para un resultado pendiente.
questions.translation: Hemos abierto una investigación, pero todavía no hemos confirmado que la cuenta estuviera comprometida.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: Which sentence clearly separates an observed fact from an interpretation?
options: We observed a new inbox rule; we are still determining why it was created.
We observed a malicious inbox rule, although its purpose has not been determined yet.
A new inbox rule was observed, meaning that an attacker probably created it for persistence.
We saw the rule and interpreted its creation as confirmation of unauthorized access.
questions.explanation: La primera parte comunica el hecho observado; la segunda presenta la interpretación como trabajo pendiente. El punto y coma refuerza esa separación.
questions.translation: Observamos una nueva regla de bandeja de entrada; todavía estamos determinando por qué se creó.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: A report says, 'The alert was a false positive.' You want a less categorical spoken version while the review is open. Which is best?
options: So far, the activity appears to be legitimate, but the review is still in progress.
The alert is probably false because we have not found anything malicious yet.
At this time, the alert can be called a false positive unless new evidence changes it.
So far, the activity is legitimate, although we cannot completely guarantee that conclusion.
questions.explanation: «Appears to be» y «still in progress» comunican una valoración provisional. La frase evita etiquetar definitivamente el caso antes de terminar la revisión.
questions.translation: Por ahora, la actividad parece legítima, pero la revisión sigue en curso.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: Select the clearest explanation of the difference between an event and an alert.
options: An event is raw information, whereas an alert confirms that the event is relevant and malicious.
Events happen first and alerts happen later, which is the main difference between the terms.
An event records an action, while an alert is the incident created from that action.
An event records something that happened; an alert indicates that the activity matched defined conditions.
questions.explanation: El paralelismo «An event...; an alert...» facilita la comparación. «Matched defined conditions» describe el concepto sin equipararlo a malicia confirmada.
questions.translation: Un evento registra algo que ocurrió; una alerta indica que la actividad cumplió unas condiciones definidas.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: During a call, you need to say that one alert added supporting information. Which phrase is most natural?
options: The second alert confirmed the entire investigation.
The second alert provided additional context for the investigation.
The second alert provided us more context to make the incident become confirmed.
The second alert was a context for the investigation and supported all its conclusions.
questions.explanation: «Provide additional context» es una colocación muy natural. «Evidence» es incontable y no debe usarse como «an evidence».
questions.translation: La segunda alerta aportó contexto adicional para la investigación.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: Which customer update uses 'evidence' correctly?
options: We have found an evidence of unauthorized access, but its scope needs more informations.
We have found several evidences, which conclusively confirms the full scope and impact of the unauthorized access.
We found enough evidences to know that every affected system was accessed.
We have found some evidence of unauthorized access, but we need more information about its scope.
questions.explanation: «Evidence» e «information» son incontables en este uso: «some evidence» y «more information». El contraste mantiene separadas existencia y alcance.
questions.translation: Hemos encontrado indicios de acceso no autorizado, pero necesitamos más información sobre su alcance.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: The SOC has escalated an alert for deeper analysis. Which explanation is most customer-friendly?
options: We escalated the alert, so the breach is serious enough to require deeper technical investigation.
The alert was escalated due to its confirmation needing a much more detailed review by the appropriate technical specialists.
Escalation means that the first analyst could not decide whether the incident was real.
We escalated the alert because it requires a more detailed review, not because a breach has been confirmed.
questions.explanation: La estructura «not because...» anticipa y corrige una posible interpretación. «Requires a more detailed review» explica el motivo sin culpar ni exagerar.
questions.translation: Escalamos la alerta porque requiere una revisión más detallada, no porque se haya confirmado una brecha.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · Alerts, evidence and incidents
questions.question: Choose the best spoken summary when no incident has been confirmed.
options: At this stage, this is not an incident, because alerts cannot become incidents until closure.
For the moment, we only have an alert and therefore there is no security concern.
At this stage, we have an alert under investigation rather than a confirmed incident.
Currently, we have an investigated alert instead of an incident that has been confirmed.
questions.explanation: «At this stage» y «rather than» contrastan dos estados de forma natural. La frase no minimiza la señal ni presenta reglas técnicas innecesarias.
questions.translation: En esta fase, tenemos una alerta en investigación, no un incidente confirmado.

questions.question: You are explaining correlation to a non-technical audience. Which version is clearest?
options: Correlation joins events and therefore proves that they were produced by the same attacker.
Correlation brings related events together so that analysts can assess the broader context.
Correlation is the action of correlating events for obtaining a context that is broader.
Correlation converts several low-level events into one confirmed high-level incident.
questions.explanation: «Brings ... together» es accesible en lenguaje oral y «so that» explica el propósito. No se promete que la relación esté confirmada.
questions.translation: La correlación reúne eventos relacionados para que los analistas puedan evaluar el contexto general.

questions.question: Complete the explanation: 'Individually, these events may look harmless; ___.'
options: together, they form a pattern worth investigating
together, they definitely prove a compromise
when together, they are making a pattern that deserves to investigate
collectively, the incident is automatically confirmed by their existence
questions.explanation: El adverbio «together» crea un contraste claro con «individually». «Worth + -ing» es la estructura natural: «worth investigating».
questions.translation: Por separado, estos eventos pueden parecer inofensivos; juntos forman un patrón que merece ser investigado.

questions.question: Which sentence most naturally explains why user context matters?
options: The context of the user helps us to decide if the account has certainly been compromised.
User context helps us decide whether the activity is unusual for that particular account.
User context decides whether activity is normal and removes the need for further review.
The user's context is important because unusual activity is always malicious for that account.
questions.explanation: «Helps us decide whether...» expresa apoyo al análisis, no una decisión automática. «For that particular account» aclara la referencia.
questions.translation: El contexto del usuario nos ayuda a decidir si la actividad es inusual para esa cuenta concreta.

questions.question: A customer asks why the rule considers timing. Select the best answer.
options: The timing confirms that events occurring close together always belong to the same single attack sequence.
Time is considered for knowing if all events happened as part of one malicious activity.
The timing helps us understand whether the events could reasonably be part of the same sequence.
The rule uses timing because events outside its window are not relevant to security.
questions.explanation: «Could reasonably be» combina posibilidad y evaluación. La estructura explica la función del tiempo sin formular una regla absoluta.
questions.translation: El momento en que ocurrieron nos ayuda a entender si los eventos podrían formar razonablemente parte de la misma secuencia.

questions.question: You need to explain why asset information was added to an alert. Which sentence is best?
options: Asset information determines the required response.
The information of the asset gives context over the role and the importance of the system.
Asset data makes the alert more important because the system has a business function.
Asset information gives us context about the system's role and importance.
questions.explanation: «Gives us context about» es una colocación natural. La frase explica qué aporta la información sin afirmar que decide automáticamente la respuesta.
questions.translation: La información del activo nos aporta contexto sobre la función y la importancia del sistema.

questions.question: Which transition works best before explaining a sequence of correlated events?
options: Let me explain you how the events have connection among themselves.
I will now enumerate all correlated events in their complete technical order.
Let me walk you through how the events connect.
Let's prove the relationship by reviewing each event.
questions.explanation: «Walk someone through» es una expresión oral natural para guiar una explicación. «Explain» requeriría «explain to you», no «explain you».
questions.translation: Permitidme explicar paso a paso cómo se conectan los eventos.

questions.question: A diagram shows three stages. Choose the most natural signposting language.
options: In first place we see the sign-in, after the change, and at last the connection going outbound.
Firstly there is a sign-in; secondly, a change; and in the final, a connection is outbound.
First we see the sign-in, then the configuration change, and finally the outbound connection.
The sign-in is first, the configuration change is posterior, and the outbound connection closes.
questions.explanation: «First..., then..., and finally...» es la secuencia oral más clara y natural. Evita calcos como «in first place» o «posterior».
questions.translation: Primero vemos el inicio de sesión, después el cambio de configuración y, por último, la conexión saliente.

questions.question: Select the best way to say that two alerts share a common element.
options: Both alerts involve the same account, although they were generated by different rules.
Both alerts are involving the same account, despite being generated from different detections.
The alerts share one account, so they must represent different stages of the same incident.
Both alerts have the same account in common and therefore confirm each other's findings.
questions.explanation: El presente simple «involve» describe una relación estable. «Although» marca el contraste entre elemento común y reglas distintas.
questions.translation: Ambas alertas afectan a la misma cuenta, aunque fueron generadas por reglas diferentes.

questions.question: You want to avoid overstating a correlation. Which sentence is most appropriate?
options: The shared IP establishes a link, although we cannot yet explain exactly what the link means.
The shared IP suggests a possible link, but it is not enough to establish one on its own.
There may be a link because the IP is shared, so we can treat the activity as related.
The common IP is insufficient evidence and should not be considered during the investigation.
questions.explanation: «Suggests a possible link» expresa indicio; «not enough ... on its own» limita el valor de un único dato sin descartarlo.
questions.translation: La IP compartida sugiere un posible vínculo, pero por sí sola no basta para establecerlo.

questions.question: Which spoken summary best connects context with the next step?
options: Taken together, the events justify confirming the incident and checking the account afterwards.
By taking the events together, a closer review is justified for checking all associated account activities.
All events combined make the account suspicious, which is why its activity is considered malicious.
Taken together, the events justify a closer review, so we are checking the associated account activity.
questions.explanation: «Taken together» resume la combinación de señales y «so» introduce el siguiente paso. La formulación es prudente y fluida.
questions.translation: Considerados en conjunto, los eventos justifican una revisión más detallada, así que estamos comprobando la actividad asociada a la cuenta.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: A client asks what a false positive is. Which definition is clearest?
options: A false positive is an incorrect rule that generates unnecessary alerts without any valid technical reason.
A false positive is an alert triggered by activity that turns out to be legitimate.
A false positive happens when legitimate activity has triggered a confirmed incident.
A false positive means the analyst made a mistake while reviewing normal behavior.
questions.explanation: La definición usa la estructura natural «an alert triggered by...» y «turns out to be» para el resultado de la revisión, sin culpar a la regla ni al analista.
questions.translation: Un falso positivo es una alerta activada por una actividad que finalmente resulta ser legítima.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: Choose the best way to explain that tuning should reduce noise without hiding risk.
options: The aim is to reduce unnecessary alerts while preserving meaningful coverage.
The aim is to eliminate unnecessary alerts.
Tuning should remove noisy activity, even if some relevant alerts are no longer generated.
The objective consists in reducing alerts while keeping every possible detection unchanged.
questions.explanation: «The aim is to...» es idiomático; «while preserving» expresa dos objetivos simultáneos. La frase evita promesas imposibles.
questions.translation: El objetivo es reducir las alertas innecesarias manteniendo una cobertura significativa.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: During a review, you want to say that a recurring alert has a known explanation. Which sentence is most natural?
options: This alert normally triggers due to the scanning activity which has approval from the customer.
This alert is usually triggered by the approved scanning activity.
This approved scan always creates a false positive.
This alert has a known reason and consequently does not require any future assessment.
questions.explanation: La pasiva «is usually triggered by» es natural para explicar la causa habitual. «Usually» deja espacio para revisar cada caso.
questions.translation: Esta alerta suele activarse por la actividad de escaneo autorizada.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: A customer proposes disabling a noisy rule. Which response is polite and balanced?
options: We should not disable it because noisy rules may still detect something important in the future that other controls could miss.
Before we disable it, let's review what coverage we might lose and whether a narrower exception would help.
Disabling the rule is a bad idea; the correct solution is to create an exception instead.
Let's disable it temporarily and assume the remaining controls will provide equivalent coverage.
questions.explanation: «Before we..., let's...» propone una secuencia colaborativa. «Might» y «whether» abren opciones sin imponer una decisión técnica.
questions.translation: Antes de deshabilitarla, revisemos qué cobertura podríamos perder y si una excepción más específica sería útil.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: Which sentence best describes an exception without implying that all similar activity is safe?
options: The exception proves that this process and any similar process can be treated as safe.
The exception makes similar processes safe.
The exception is applied for avoiding alerts from processes considered legitimate in general.
The exception applies only to this approved process under the specified conditions.
questions.explanation: «Applies only to» delimita el alcance y «under the specified conditions» evita una generalización. «Excepted from monitoring» suena menos natural aquí.
questions.translation: La excepción se aplica únicamente a este proceso autorizado en las condiciones especificadas.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: Complete the update: 'Since the change was introduced, the number of duplicate alerts ___.'
options: fell since introduction
has fallen significantly
has been fallen in a significant amount
is decreasing significantly yesterday
questions.explanation: «Since» conecta un punto pasado con el presente, por lo que usamos present perfect: «has fallen». «Fall» es intransitivo y no admite «has been fallen».
questions.translation: Desde que se introdujo el cambio, el número de alertas duplicadas ha disminuido considerablemente.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: Choose the most natural way to ask whether a tuning change worked.
options: Did we reduce the noise without missing activity since the change has been applied?
Have we eliminated the noise completely?
Are we reducing the noise without having missed every activity which continues being important?
Have we reduced the noise without missing activity that still matters?
questions.explanation: Present perfect pregunta por el resultado actual de un cambio. «Activity that still matters» suena natural y no exige una garantía absoluta.
questions.translation: ¿Hemos reducido el ruido sin dejar de detectar actividad que sigue siendo relevante?

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: A chart shows fewer alerts after tuning. Which interpretation is appropriately cautious?
options: The decrease proves that the tuning was successful because fewer alerts always mean better quality.
The number has decreased, so the rule now produces only relevant alerts for the analysts.
The decrease is encouraging, but we also need to check whether detection quality has been maintained.
The decrease is positive, although it tells us that some malicious activity may have been missed.
questions.explanation: «Encouraging, but...» reconoce el resultado y añade una comprobación necesaria. Evita convertir una sola métrica en una conclusión definitiva.
questions.translation: La disminución es alentadora, pero también debemos comprobar si se ha mantenido la calidad de la detección.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: Which phrase is most natural when you do not want to label an alert as 'noise' too early?
options: It may be benign activity, but we should verify the context before closing it.
It is probably noise, so we can close it unless the customer objects to that conclusion.
It may be a false positive, but verifying it would not change the likely outcome.
This activity looks benign and consequently does not need context before being closed.
questions.explanation: «May be» expresa posibilidad y «before + -ing» fija un orden claro. La frase mantiene la prudencia sin resultar alarmista.
questions.translation: Puede tratarse de una actividad legítima, pero deberíamos verificar el contexto antes de cerrarla.

questions.topic: Explaining detections · False positives and tuning
questions.question: You are summarizing a tuning decision. Select the clearest wording.
options: We agreed on making the change permanent after monitoring its immediate result for two weeks.
The change will be permanent, although we are going to review whether it should stay in place.
We agreed to monitor the change for two weeks and review the results before making it permanent.
We agreed to a two-week monitoring, after which the tuning is assumed to be correct.
questions.explanation: El paralelismo «to monitor... and review...» resume dos acciones acordadas. «Before making it permanent» deja clara la condición.
questions.translation: Acordamos monitorizar el cambio durante dos semanas y revisar los resultados antes de hacerlo permanente.

questions.question: You are describing the first step after an alert arrives. Which sentence sounds most natural?
options: Firstly, we check if the alert is containing sufficient informations for making an assessment.
We first check whether the alert contains enough information for an initial assessment.
We first decide whether the alert is malicious.
The first step confirms whether the alert has enough evidence to become an incident.
questions.explanation: «First» es natural en lenguaje oral; «information» es incontable. «For an initial assessment» describe el propósito sin adelantar la conclusión.
questions.translation: Primero comprobamos si la alerta contiene suficiente información para una evaluación inicial.

questions.question: Which sentence explains triage in customer-friendly English?
options: Triage is when analysts classify alerts as true or false before any investigation starts.
Triage helps for prioritizing the alerts and deciding which ones need to be investigated furtherly.
Triage helps us prioritize alerts and decide which ones need further investigation.
Triage gives every alert a final severity.
questions.explanation: «Helps us prioritize... and decide...» usa verbos paralelos y lenguaje accesible. «Further» funciona como adverbio; «furtherly» no es natural.
questions.translation: El triaje nos ayuda a priorizar las alertas y decidir cuáles necesitan más investigación.

questions.question: Complete the process description: 'Before escalating the case, the analyst ___.'
options: is reviewing every possible source and confirms the final conclusion
reviews the available context and records the initial findings
makes a review of the context and writes down all definitive findings
confirms every finding before escalation
questions.explanation: El presente simple describe un proceso habitual. «Reviews... and records...» mantiene el paralelismo y usa colocaciones naturales.
questions.translation: Antes de escalar el caso, el analista revisa el contexto disponible y registra los hallazgos iniciales.

questions.question: A client asks why the analyst contacted the user. Choose the clearest response.
options: We contacted with the user for confirming if they had performed the malicious activity.
We contacted the user because their answer would prove whether the alert was a false positive.
We contacted the user to confirm whether the activity was expected.
We contacted the user to assign responsibility.
questions.explanation: En inglés se dice «contacted the user», sin «with». «To confirm whether...» expresa el propósito de forma neutral.
questions.translation: Contactamos con el usuario para confirmar si la actividad era esperada.

questions.question: Which update distinguishes what has been checked from what remains to be checked?
options: We verified the owner already, and the device activity is being pending for review.
We have checked the account owner and therefore only the device remains unverified.
We have verified the account owner; we are still reviewing the device activity.
The owner is verified, while the device activity has not provided a conclusion yet.
questions.explanation: Present perfect comunica un resultado actual; present continuous describe el trabajo en curso. El punto y coma separa ambos estados con claridad.
questions.translation: Hemos verificado al titular de la cuenta; todavía estamos revisando la actividad del dispositivo.

questions.question: During a handover, which sentence most clearly states an outstanding task?
options: The next analyst keeps pending to confirm from where the connection originated.
The connection source should be confirmed if the next analyst considers it necessary.
Confirmation of the connection source remains, but it is probably not important now.
The next analyst still needs to confirm the source of the connection.
questions.explanation: «Still needs to + infinitive» expresa una tarea pendiente de manera directa. Evita el calco «keeps pending».
questions.translation: El siguiente analista todavía tiene que confirmar el origen de la conexión.

questions.question: Choose the most natural way to describe a completed validation step.
options: We proved the hash had a malicious reputation.
The hash was contrasted against the intelligence sources that were available to us.
We made a checking of the hash in the threat intelligence sources we currently use.
We checked the hash against our available threat intelligence sources.
questions.explanation: «Check X against Y» es la colocación habitual. El past simple presenta una acción terminada sin añadir un resultado no mencionado.
questions.translation: Comprobamos el hash con las fuentes de inteligencia de amenazas disponibles.

questions.question: A customer asks for an immediate conclusion while triage is still under way. Which response is best?
options: We can give you a preliminary view now, but we will need more time for a firm conclusion.
We can provide a firm conclusion now, although it may need to be completely changed after the remaining triage checks.
It is too early to say anything useful, so we should wait until every check is finished.
Our preliminary view is likely correct, and the remaining checks are mainly procedural.
questions.explanation: «Preliminary view» frente a «firm conclusion» establece dos niveles de certeza. El tono es colaborativo y no bloquea la comunicación.
questions.translation: Podemos daros ahora una valoración preliminar, pero necesitaremos más tiempo para llegar a una conclusión firme.

questions.question: Which sentence best explains why an alert was closed after validation?
options: The activity matched an approved administrative task, and we found no additional signs of concern.
The administrator confirmed the activity, so no other evidence needed to be reviewed before closure.
The alert matched an administrative task and was therefore automatically considered harmless.
We closed the alert because approved tasks cannot create behavior that looks suspicious.
questions.explanation: «Matched an approved task» y «found no additional signs» ofrecen una explicación clara. La conjunción «and» une dos razones sin formular absolutos.
questions.translation: La actividad coincidía con una tarea administrativa autorizada y no encontramos otros indicios preocupantes.

questions.question: Select the best spoken transition from triage results to next steps.
options: Now that the checks are covered, I will explain you the actions we will realize next.
Now that we've covered the initial checks, let me explain what we are doing next.
Having completed triage, the subsequent procedural activities will now be enumerated.
The checks are finished, so the next steps will confirm the final result of the investigation.
questions.explanation: «Now that we've covered...» y «let me explain...» son marcadores orales naturales. «Explain you» y «realize actions» son calcos.
questions.translation: Ahora que hemos repasado las comprobaciones iniciales, permitidme explicar qué estamos haciendo a continuación.

questions.question: You need to explain why a case was escalated. Which sentence is clearest?
options: We escalated the case due to the activity requiring a specialist to confirm the attack.
We escalated the case to confirm the attack.
Escalation was made so a specialist can decide the incident is genuinely malicious.
We escalated the case because the activity requires specialist review.
questions.explanation: «Escalated the case because...» es directo y neutral. «Requires specialist review» explica la necesidad sin criticar a otro analista ni anticipar el resultado.
questions.translation: Escalamos el caso porque la actividad requiere una revisión especializada.

questions.question: Which phrase best reassures a customer that the handoff will preserve context?
options: The notes contain everything, so the next team will not need to repeat any checks.
All context has been written in the case, guaranteeing a seamless handoff without questions.
The case notes include the checks completed so far and the reasons for escalation.
The case notes explain the escalation, while completed checks can be discussed if required.
questions.explanation: «Include the checks... and the reasons...» enumera contenido concreto. Evita promesas absolutas como «everything» o «guaranteeing».
questions.translation: Las notas del caso incluyen las comprobaciones realizadas hasta ahora y los motivos del escalado.

questions.question: Complete the handoff message: 'Could you review the endpoint activity and ___?'
options: confirm whether persistence is definitely established
advise us whether the endpoint is compromised in every possible way
say us if you can see a persistence mechanism being certainly present
let us know whether you see any signs of persistence
questions.explanation: «Let us know whether...» es una petición natural y colaborativa. En inglés no se usa «say us»; sería «tell us».
questions.translation: ¿Podríais revisar la actividad del endpoint y decirnos si observáis algún indicio de persistencia?

questions.question: A client asks whether escalation means the situation is severe. Choose the best response.
options: No, escalation is only a workflow step and has no relationship with potential severity.
Usually yes, because specialists only receive cases that are likely to become incidents.
Not necessarily; it means the case needs a different level of expertise or access.
It means the situation may be severe, although escalation confirms nothing except concern.
questions.explanation: «Not necessarily» corrige sin ser tajante. La explicación usa «a different level of...» para describir la razón con claridad.
questions.translation: No necesariamente; significa que el caso requiere un nivel diferente de conocimientos o acceso.

questions.question: Which sentence politely asks another team for an estimated response time?
options: Can you confirm the exact time when the review will be completed without further delay?
Please tell us how much time you will spend before giving the final answer.
Would you communicate an estimation for the review to become completed?
Could you let us know when you expect to complete the review?
questions.explanation: «Could you let us know...» suaviza la petición y «when you expect to...» solicita una previsión, no una garantía.
questions.translation: ¿Podríais indicarnos cuándo esperáis completar la revisión?

questions.question: You are updating the customer after a delayed handoff. Which wording takes ownership without blaming?
options: The receiving team has delayed the handoff unexpectedly, but we have asked them to prioritize the case and respond soon.
The handoff was late because another team did not respond within the expected timeframe.
The handoff took longer than expected, and we are working with the receiving team to move the review forward.
There has been a delay outside the SOC, and responsibility is currently being clarified.
questions.explanation: La frase usa «took longer than expected» para reconocer el retraso y se centra en la acción actual. Evita atribuir culpa.
questions.translation: El traspaso tardó más de lo previsto y estamos trabajando con el equipo receptor para hacer avanzar la revisión.

questions.question: Select the clearest way to state who owns the next action.
options: The identity team will verify the account settings, and the SOC will track the case to completion.
The identity team owns the account settings, while the SOC owns ensuring that every required action is completed.
Account verification belongs to identity, and tracking belongs to us until all issues disappear.
The SOC passes the action to identity but continues to be responsible for their response.
questions.explanation: Dos sujetos explícitos y dos verbos paralelos hacen inequívoca la responsabilidad. «Track the case to completion» es una colocación profesional.
questions.translation: El equipo de identidad verificará la configuración de la cuenta y el SOC hará seguimiento del caso hasta su finalización.

questions.question: A specialist requests more context. Which reply is most concise and useful?
options: I will provide all the context that exists so you can make a definitive determination.
The requested context will be added after I collect every potentially relevant detail.
I'll add the relevant timeline and user details to the case notes now.
I'll send more information, although most of it is already available in several tools.
questions.explanation: «I'll ... now» promete una acción concreta e inmediata. «Relevant timeline and user details» especifica qué se añadirá sin exceso de palabras.
questions.translation: Añadiré ahora a las notas del caso la cronología y los datos relevantes del usuario.

questions.question: Which summary makes the handoff status clear to a customer?
options: The case has been assigned to the endpoint team, and their review is now in progress.
The endpoint team has the case, so a conclusion should be available very shortly.
The case was passed to endpoint and is waiting for them to start working on it now.
The endpoint review is in progress, which means the escalation stage is almost complete.
questions.explanation: Present perfect («has been assigned») comunica el estado actual; present continuous («is ... in progress») describe la actividad en curso.
questions.translation: El caso se ha asignado al equipo de endpoint y su revisión ya está en curso.

questions.question: You want to close a handoff call by confirming alignment. Which question sounds most natural?
options: Is everything covered so you can continue without needing anything else from our side?
Have we given enough information for you to accept full responsibility for the next stage?
Do you confirm that our part is finished?
Does that cover everything you need from us before you continue the review?
questions.explanation: «Does that cover everything you need...?» es una pregunta colaborativa y natural. Confirma suficiencia sin descargar responsabilidad.
questions.translation: ¿Con esto queda cubierto todo lo que necesitáis de nuestra parte antes de continuar la revisión?

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: Choose the most natural opening for a monitoring update.
options: Since our last update, we have not observed any further suspicious activity.
From our last update, we did not observe more suspicious activities until the present moment.
Since the last update, no activity has occurred.
After our update, the monitoring has proved that the environment is now fully secure.
questions.explanation: «Since» pide present perfect para un periodo conectado con el presente. «Activity» es normalmente incontable en este contexto.
questions.translation: Desde nuestra última actualización no hemos observado más actividad sospechosa.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: A customer asks what continuous monitoring means. Which answer is clearest?
options: It means that an analyst watches every event continuously, in real time and without any interruption throughout the day.
It means that relevant activity is reviewed on an ongoing basis rather than only at fixed intervals.
Continuous monitoring means the tools guarantee immediate detection at all times.
It is monitoring that continues because all relevant activity must be manually reviewed.
questions.explanation: «On an ongoing basis rather than...» define el concepto mediante contraste. Evita interpretar «continuous» como vigilancia humana absoluta.
questions.translation: Significa que la actividad relevante se revisa de forma continua, no solo a intervalos fijos.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: Complete the status update: 'We are continuing to monitor the account ___.'
options: in case that malicious activity will definitely return
for detecting if the attacker is going to come back again
for any signs of renewed activity
until we can guarantee security
questions.explanation: La colocación natural es «monitor X for signs of Y». «Renewed activity» expresa reaparición sin afirmar que ocurrirá.
questions.translation: Seguimos monitorizando la cuenta por si aparecen indicios de nueva actividad.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: Which sentence explains a scheduled review most naturally?
options: We will revise the trend at week end.
We are reviewing the alert trend at week end, when its final result will be known.
The trend will be revised by us again after all alerts for the week have finished.
We will review the alert trend again at the end of the week.
questions.explanation: «Review the trend» y «at the end of the week» son expresiones naturales. «Revision» y «tendency» suelen ser falsos amigos en este contexto.
questions.translation: Volveremos a revisar la tendencia de las alertas al final de la semana.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: A chart fluctuates from day to day. Choose the most careful interpretation.
options: The daily figures vary, but there is no clear upward or downward trend yet.
The figures change every day, which means the trend is unstable and cannot be useful.
Daily variation indicates that alert volume is both increasing and decreasing over time.
The chart has no trend because the values have not remained constant each day.
questions.explanation: «Vary» describe cambios; «no clear ... yet» comunica que todavía no hay dirección evidente. No confunde variación con inutilidad.
questions.translation: Las cifras diarias varían, pero todavía no hay una tendencia clara al alza o a la baja.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: You need to say that a watch period has finished. Which sentence is most natural?
options: The monitoring period has finished now after seven full days without the activity repeating again.
Seven days of monitoring have ended and prove that the activity cannot recur.
The watch period is completed, so recurrence has been ruled out permanently.
The seven-day monitoring period has now ended, and we found no recurrence of the activity.
questions.explanation: Present perfect con «has now ended» destaca el estado actual. «Found no recurrence» informa del resultado limitado al periodo.
questions.translation: El periodo de monitorización de siete días ya ha terminado y no observamos que la actividad se repitiera.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: Which update makes a change of plan explicit without sounding disorganized?
options: We changed the plan because the previous monitoring period was not sufficient for anything.
Based on the new information, we are extending the monitoring period by 48 hours.
New information forces us to monitor for 48 more hours than we originally should have done.
The plan has changed again, and monitoring will continue until we feel more confident.
questions.explanation: «Based on...» introduce la razón y «extend ... by 48 hours» expresa exactamente el cambio. El tono transmite adaptación, no improvisación.
questions.translation: A partir de la nueva información, ampliaremos el periodo de monitorización en 48 horas.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: Select the best way to report that an alert volume returned to normal.
options: The alert volume returned to normality.
Alerts are normal again, so yesterday's increase can be treated as irrelevant.
The volume has normalized, proving that the temporary increase had no security impact.
Alert volume has returned to its usual range after yesterday's increase.
questions.explanation: «Alert volume» y «usual range» son colocaciones naturales. Present perfect conecta el retorno con la situación actual.
questions.translation: El volumen de alertas ha vuelto a su rango habitual tras el aumento de ayer.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: A customer asks whether monitoring can stop. Which answer is balanced and clear?
options: We can stop monitoring because the absence of alerts confirms that the risk has disappeared.
Additional monitoring should continue indefinitely in case the same activity ever returns.
We can stop the additional monitoring as planned, while the standard controls remain in place.
The monitoring can stop, although doing so will remove all visibility of the account.
questions.explanation: La frase diferencia «additional monitoring» de «standard controls». «As planned» confirma el acuerdo sin afirmar riesgo cero.
questions.translation: Podemos finalizar la monitorización adicional según lo previsto, mientras los controles habituales siguen activos.

questions.topic: SOC process · Monitoring and status updates
questions.question: Which closing sentence works best at the end of a routine status update?
options: We will keep monitoring everything and immediately report every change we can observe.
We'll continue to monitor the situation and let you know if anything material changes.
We will continue the monitoring until there is certainty that nothing else can happen.
If something changes, we may provide another update when the investigation requires it.
questions.explanation: «Let you know if anything material changes» es profesional y concreto. «Material» limita las actualizaciones a cambios relevantes.
questions.translation: Seguiremos monitorizando la situación y os informaremos si se produce algún cambio relevante.

questions.question: You cannot confirm whether data was accessed. Which sentence is most precise?
options: The logs do not show file access, so we can confirm that the files were not accessed.
The available logs do not allow us to confirm whether the files were accessed.
We cannot confirm access because the files probably were not opened by the attacker.
There is no evidence of access, which is equivalent to evidence that no access occurred.
questions.explanation: «Do not allow us to confirm whether...» describe un límite probatorio sin convertir ausencia de evidencia en evidencia de ausencia.
questions.translation: Los registros disponibles no nos permiten confirmar si se accedió a los archivos.

questions.question: Choose the best way to state a moderate-confidence assessment.
options: We believe the activity is likely related, although we cannot confirm the link yet.
We are moderately certain that the activity is related, so the link can be treated as established.
The activity must be related, although some confirmation is still technically pending.
We think there is a relationship and will assume it is confirmed unless contrary evidence appears.
questions.explanation: «We believe... likely» comunica una valoración; «although» introduce la limitación. «Yet» indica que la confirmación puede llegar después.
questions.translation: Creemos que la actividad probablemente está relacionada, aunque todavía no podemos confirmar el vínculo.

questions.question: A customer asks for a guarantee that the activity has stopped. Which response is most professional?
options: We have seen no further activity, but we cannot guarantee that it will not recur.
We guarantee that the activity has stopped because no new alerts have been generated.
The activity appears to have stopped, so recurrence is now extremely unlikely in all cases.
We cannot guarantee anything, which is why monitoring results should not be relied upon.
questions.explanation: La frase distingue observación y garantía. «Cannot guarantee that it will not recur» expresa el límite sin invalidar lo observado.
questions.translation: No hemos visto más actividad, pero no podemos garantizar que no vuelva a producirse.

questions.question: Which phrase best introduces an assumption in a presentation?
options: This assessment believes the account inventory to be complete and currently updated.
We know the inventory is complete, unless information not yet available proves otherwise.
This assessment assumes that the account inventory is complete and up to date.
The assessment is correct provided that no account is missing for any possible reason.
questions.explanation: «This assessment assumes that...» hace explícito el supuesto. «Up to date» es la expresión idiomática para información actualizada.
questions.translation: Esta evaluación presupone que el inventario de cuentas está completo y actualizado.

questions.question: You need to correct an overly certain slide title: 'No data was exfiltrated.' Which replacement is safest?
options: No evidence of data exfiltration was identified in the available sources.
Data exfiltration did not occur according to all currently available evidence.
The investigation confirms that no data was exfiltrated from the monitored environment.
No exfiltration was identified, meaning that the data remained inside the organization.
questions.explanation: La pasiva «was identified» limita la afirmación a lo observado. «In the available sources» hace explícito el alcance de la evidencia.
questions.translation: No se identificaron indicios de exfiltración de datos en las fuentes disponibles.

questions.question: A client asks why your conclusion may change. Which explanation is clearest?
options: Our assessment may change if new evidence becomes available.
Our conclusion may change because the evidence is incomplete.
The assessment is temporary and will probably change when more data is reviewed.
Any conclusion can change, so the current assessment should not guide decisions.
questions.explanation: «May change if...» expresa una condición posible sin debilitar innecesariamente la evaluación actual. «Evidence becomes available» es una colocación natural.
questions.translation: Nuestra evaluación puede cambiar si aparecen nuevas evidencias.

questions.question: Select the most natural way to say that two explanations remain possible.
options: At this point, both explanations continue being possible and equally correct.
Both explanations are equally likely.
For now, the two explanations have the same probability and cannot be distinguished.
At this point, both explanations remain plausible.
questions.explanation: «Remain plausible» es conciso y no afirma que las opciones sean igual de probables. «At this point» sitúa la valoración en el momento actual.
questions.translation: En este momento, ambas explicaciones siguen siendo plausibles.

questions.question: Which sentence clearly communicates a low-confidence finding?
options: We have a low-confidence attribution, which means the possible match is probably correct but still incomplete.
The evidence gives a possible match and therefore supports naming the likely actor cautiously.
We have a possible match, but the evidence is too limited for a confident attribution.
We cannot attribute the activity, so the possible match has no analytical value.
questions.explanation: «Possible match» y «too limited for...» explican por qué no se puede llegar a una atribución firme. La frase evita tanto exagerar como descartar.
questions.translation: Tenemos una posible coincidencia, pero la evidencia es demasiado limitada para realizar una atribución con confianza.

questions.question: You want to distinguish 'unknown' from 'not applicable.' Which wording is clearest?
options: The answer is not applicable because it is unknown.
We do not know the answer, so the question cannot be applied to this investigation.
The answer remains unknown and should therefore be recorded as not applicable for now.
The answer is currently unknown; that does not mean the question is irrelevant.
questions.explanation: El punto y coma separa dos ideas y «that does not mean...» evita equiparar falta de información con irrelevancia.
questions.translation: La respuesta se desconoce actualmente; eso no significa que la pregunta sea irrelevante.

questions.question: Choose the best closing statement for an uncertain finding.
options: This is the best conclusion, and it will remain valid unless somebody disproves it.
Based on today's information, this assessment is as certain as the evidence permits completely.
This is our current, mainly speculative opinion.
This is our best assessment based on the information available today.
questions.explanation: «Best assessment based on...» transmite rigor y limita la conclusión a la información disponible. No suena defensivo ni excesivamente débil.
questions.translation: Esta es nuestra mejor evaluación a partir de la información disponible hoy.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: You need to summarize a detection in one sentence for an executive. Which version is best?
options: The detection found an account anomaly that was investigated and did not become a confirmed breach.
An unusual account generated an alert, but a compromise has not been conclusively proven by the SOC so far.
The alert highlighted unusual account activity, and the review has not found evidence of compromise so far.
The alert was suspicious, although the investigation currently considers the account completely safe.
questions.explanation: La frase resume señal y estado actual. «So far» conserva la prudencia; «has not found evidence» no equivale a afirmar que el compromiso sea imposible.
questions.translation: La alerta señaló una actividad inusual en la cuenta y, por ahora, la revisión no ha encontrado indicios de compromiso.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: Which transition moves naturally from findings to recommendations?
options: After explaining all the observations, we will now change the subject and move directly to the final recommendations.
Now that we've covered what we observed, let's turn to the recommended next steps.
The findings are finished, so the actions that must be implemented come next.
Having covered the evidence, recommendations will be spoken about in the following section.
questions.explanation: «Now that we've covered...» y «let's turn to...» son marcadores orales naturales. Introducen la siguiente sección sin sonar rígidos.
questions.translation: Ahora que hemos repasado lo observado, pasemos a los próximos pasos recomendados.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: A slide contains too much technical detail. Which spoken summary is clearest?
options: The key point is the technical investigation, whose details prove that no customer action will ever be needed.
In summary, many checks were completed and the alert can now be forgotten by the customer.
The important thing is that our process worked, despite the technical details being too complex to explain.
The key point is that the alert was investigated promptly and no immediate action is required from you.
questions.explanation: «The key point is that...» enfoca el mensaje y «no immediate action is required» aclara la consecuencia actual sin promesas futuras.
questions.translation: La idea clave es que la alerta se investigó con rapidez y no se requiere ninguna acción inmediata por vuestra parte.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: Choose the most natural way to check whether the customer wants more detail.
options: Do you want that I explain you all the investigation steps in more detail?
Would it be helpful if I walked you through the investigation steps?
Do you want a full technical explanation?
Is it necessary for me to enumerate the steps so the investigation can be understood?
questions.explanation: Después de «Would it be helpful if...?» usamos pasado simple con sentido hipotético. «Walk you through» es natural al ofrecer una explicación guiada.
questions.translation: ¿Os resultaría útil que repasara con vosotros los pasos de la investigación?

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: A customer asks for the practical impact. Which answer is most direct?
options: At present, users and operations have not been impacted in any possible way.
At present, there is no identified impact on users or business operations.
There is no impact because no incident was confirmed.
No business impact has been identified, which confirms that the activity was harmless.
questions.explanation: «No identified impact» limita la afirmación a lo observado. «At present» deja claro que se trata del estado actual.
questions.translation: Actualmente no se ha identificado impacto en los usuarios ni en las operaciones del negocio.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: Which sentence assigns a next step without sounding commanding?
options: You need to review the account immediately and remove its access unless it can be justified.
The account access should be removed because reviewing whether it is required would take too long.
We recommend reviewing the affected account's access and confirming that it is still required.
Our recommendation is that you must confirm the account and all its permissions today.
questions.explanation: «We recommend + -ing» formula una recomendación profesional. Las dos acciones paralelas son claras y no imponen una urgencia no indicada.
questions.translation: Recomendamos revisar los accesos de la cuenta afectada y confirmar que siguen siendo necesarios.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: You want to state when the next update will arrive. Choose the clearest wording.
options: We will send the next update by 3 p.m., even if there is no material change.
We will send an update around 3 p.m. if we have something important enough to report.
The next communication will be at 3 p.m. unless the investigation remains unchanged.
We will try to provide the following update before 3 p.m., depending on the results.
questions.explanation: «By 3 p.m.» fija un límite claro y «even if» confirma que la comunicación no depende de nuevos hallazgos.
questions.translation: Enviaremos la próxima actualización antes de las 15:00, aunque no haya ningún cambio relevante.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: Which closing recap is easiest to follow in a meeting?
options: As a recap, we are reviewing an unconfirmed alert and will probably know more later today.
To summarize all points, there is no confirmed compromise because the review is still being done.
In conclusion, the alert remains open, but the scheduled update later today should provide a complete and final answer for everyone involved.
To recap, the alert is under review, no compromise has been confirmed, and the next update is due at 3 p.m.
questions.explanation: «To recap» introduce tres puntos paralelos y concretos. La frase evita prometer una conclusión final en la próxima actualización.
questions.translation: En resumen, la alerta sigue en revisión, no se ha confirmado ningún compromiso y la próxima actualización está prevista para las 15:00.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: A customer has misunderstood your conclusion. Which correction is most diplomatic?
options: That is not what I said: the absence of evidence does not prove there was no compromise.
Just to clarify, we have not found evidence of compromise; we have not ruled it out completely.
You may have misunderstood the result, because our conclusion was only provisional.
To correct the record, compromise remains possible despite the customer's interpretation.
questions.explanation: «Just to clarify» suaviza la corrección. El paralelismo «we have not...; we have not...» distingue dos afirmaciones de forma memorable.
questions.translation: Solo para aclararlo: no hemos encontrado indicios de compromiso, pero no lo hemos descartado por completo.

questions.topic: Customer briefings · Clear summaries and next steps
questions.question: Select the best final sentence after presenting recommendations.
options: If you accept our recommendations, we will assign every action and deadline to the appropriate owner.
Once the approach is agreed, the customer must document the owners and completion dates.
If there are no objections, we will consider every recommendation approved and start immediately.
If you agree with this approach, we'll document the actions and confirm the owners and dates.
questions.explanation: La condicional «If you agree...» confirma consentimiento y el paralelismo «document... and confirm...» concreta el cierre. No presupone aprobación.
questions.translation: Si estáis de acuerdo con este enfoque, documentaremos las acciones y confirmaremos responsables y fechas.
